summary:
The talk by Manish Sanwal (Director of AI, NewsCorp) addresses how to build robust, transparent, and self-correcting AI using Layered Chain of Thought (Layered CoT) prompting integrated with multi-agentic systems. Sanwal begins by introducing multi-agentic systems—collections of specialized AI agents that each handle specific tasks rather than relying on monolithic systems. Using self-driving cars as an example, he illustrates how specialized agents (pedestrian detection, traffic signal reading, route optimization) work in harmony, offering advantages in specialization, flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance.

He then explains Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting, which guides AI through step-by-step reasoning rather than jumping to conclusions. CoT provides transparency and opportunities for fine-tuning and debugging by exposing intermediate reasoning steps. However, Sanwal identifies key limitations: sensitivity to prompt phrasing affecting reproducibility, absence of real-time verification or feedback, risk of cascading errors from early flawed inferences, and potential to miss critical connections in complex multi-factor problems.

To address these limitations, Sanwal introduces Layered Chain of Thought, a two-step iterative approach: (1) generation of an initial thought, and (2) verification of that thought against a structured knowledge base or external database via fact-checking, consistency checks, or ensemble models. Only verified thoughts proceed to the next reasoning step. This iterative verification yields self-correction, robustness against prompt variability, greater reproducibility, and enhanced transparency for auditing. Sanwal notes that Layered CoT integrates seamlessly within multi-agentic systems, where each specialized agent contributes verified reasoning to a robust overall system. He concludes that the future of AI lies not in building bigger models but in creating structured, explainable, and reliable systems, referencing a published paper on Layered CoT prompting available on arXiv.

sections.title: Introduction and Speaker Background
sections.summary: Manish Sanwal, Director of AI at NewsCorp, introduces the talk on building AI that is smarter, structured, and self-correcting using Layered Chain of Thought with multi-agentic systems. He frames the core thesis: true AI is built incrementally with every step verified and refined through collaborative effort.

sections.title: Multi-Agentic Systems Overview
sections.summary: Sanwal defines multi-agentic systems as collections of specialized AI agents that work together on complex tasks instead of relying on monolithic systems. He uses self-driving cars as an example—agents for pedestrian detection, traffic signals, and routing—and highlights advantages: specialization, flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance. Adding Chain of Thought reasoning enhances transparency and resiliency.

sections.title: Chain of Thought Prompting
sections.summary: Sanwal explains Chain of Thought as a method guiding AI to reason step by step rather than guessing answers. Traditional LLMs often jump directly to conclusions. CoT breaks problems into manageable steps, providing transparency into the reasoning process and enabling fine-tuning and debugging by exposing intermediate steps for correction before the final answer.

sections.title: Limitations of Traditional Chain of Thought
sections.summary: Sanwal identifies key limitations of CoT: sensitivity to prompt phrasing affecting reproducibility, no built-in verification or real-time feedback mechanism, risk of cascading errors from early flawed inferences, and difficulty integrating all variables in complex multi-factor problems, leading to oversimplified conclusions.

sections.title: Layered Chain of Thought Approach
sections.summary: Sanwal introduces Layered CoT as a two-step iterative process: (1) generation of an initial thought from the input prompt, and (2) verification of that thought against a structured knowledge base or external database using fact-checking, consistency checks, or ensemble models. Only verified thoughts proceed, and the process repeats to build a fully confirmed reasoning chain.

sections.title: Benefits of Layered CoT
sections.summary: Layered CoT provides self-correction by catching errors early, robustness against prompt variability through independent step verification, greater reproducibility, and enhanced transparency for auditing. It transforms AI reasoning into a robust iterative framework and integrates seamlessly within multi-agentic systems where each specialized agent contributes verified reasoning.

sections.title: Conclusion and Reference
sections.summary: Sanwal concludes that the future of AI is about creating structured, explainable, and reliable systems rather than just bigger models. He references a published paper on Layered CoT prompting available on arXiv and invites audience feedback.
